sources.title: Introducing LLaMA: A foundational, 65-billion-parameter large language model
sources.evidence: February 24, 2023 announcement includes LLaMA 7B, describes text continuation, and announces noncommercial research access subject to individual approval.

sources.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
sources.evidence: Table 2 reports 6.7B parameters, width 4096, 32 heads, 32 layers and 1.0T training tokens for the 7B variant. Section 2.2 describes Transformer, RMSNorm, SwiGLU and RoPE. Sections 3.1 and 3.4 evaluate reasoning.

sources.title: Original release LLaMA version 1 model card
sources.evidence: The release-day card identifies FAIR at Meta AI, version 1, the 7B autoregressive Transformer, a foundational research model without human-feedback training, and a noncommercial bespoke license.

sources.title: Original release LLaMA Transformer implementation
sources.evidence: Implements causal multi-head attention and dense SwiGLU blocks without expert routing. The initial runtime default max_seq_len is 1024. Its header explicitly assigns GPLv3 to the software.

sources.title: Original release LLaMA README
sources.evidence: Documents application for checkpoint/tokenizer access, download links after approval, and 7B inference with model-parallel degree 1.

sources.title: Original release LLaMA generation interface
sources.evidence: The generator accepts string prompts, generation length, temperature and top-p, and returns decoded strings. It exposes neither a separate reasoning channel nor structured function/tool calls.

sources.title: Original LLaMA context-default correction
sources.evidence: The March 5, 2023 repository change raises max_seq_len from 1024 to 2048 and explains that the models support a 2048-token context window.

sources.title: Llama 2 technical report: explicit Llama 1 comparison
sources.evidence: Table 1 directly lists Llama 1 7B with 2k context, separately from Llama 2 7B at 4k. Appendix A.2.1 specifies the expansion from 2048 to 4096 tokens. Only the explicitly labeled Llama 1 evidence is used.

sources.title: Original release repository software license
sources.evidence: The repository LICENSE contains GNU GPL version 3, consistent with the source-file software notices. This does not replace the separately documented model-weight license.

name.note: Original first-generation 7B base checkpoint; not Llama 2 or an instruction-tuned derivative.

developer.note: The release card names the FAIR team of Meta AI.

family.note: The developer calls this family LLaMA; lowercase is the catalog key.

release_date.note: Public announcement and access-request opening. Weight delivery followed individual approval; no approval date is inferred. The paper appeared on arXiv three days later.

open_weights.note: Historical gated research checkpoint release. This does not imply unrestricted distribution or current application fulfillment.

license.note: Supported descriptive weight-license label. The original card says noncommercial bespoke license; GPLv3 applies to reference software. The later Llama 2 license does not apply. Full original weight-agreement terms were not separately verified.

parameters_b.note: Paper Table 2 explicitly reports 6.7B for the variant marketed as 7B. This is a rounded billions figure, not an exact checkpoint tensor census. No weights were downloaded.

active_parameters_b.note: No separate active-per-token count or counting convention is given; dense architecture does not justify copying the total.

architecture.note: Autoregressive decoder Transformer. The 7B row has 32 layers, 32 heads and width 4096; implementation uses dense attention and feed-forward blocks without expert routing.

context_window.note: Later first-party comparison explicitly gives Llama 1 7B a 2048-token context. The initial 1024-token runtime default was subsequently corrected; it was not the trained context length.

modalities.note: Text prompts and generated text; the reference interface consumes and returns strings.

reasoning.note: Reasoning benchmarks demonstrate evaluated capabilities, not a dedicated thinking mode or separate reasoning output. The base-model release specifies no such feature.

tool_call.note: No native structured tool/function-call feature is specified in the card or text-completion interface; downstream integrations are a separate question.

description.note: Accurate description of the version-1 foundational research checkpoint.

patch.notes: Original LLaMA 7B: the paper reports a rounded 6.7B total, not a tensor-exact count; active parameters are not separately disclosed. February 24, 2023 is the public announcement and access-request date; checkpoint delivery required research approval. open_weights means released gated weights, not unrestricted access. Weights use a bespoke noncommercial research license; reference software uses GPLv3. The original context is 2048 tokens. Dedicated thinking mode and native tool calling are not documented.

summary: Correct parameters from the 7B marketing label to the original paper's rounded 6.7B. Confirm original release, dense architecture, 2048 context, text modalities and research weight license. Keep active parameters, dedicated reasoning and native tool calling null because they are not separately specified. Reference code GPLv3 is distinct from the model license.
